en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga:
The Section on Saṅghādisesa Offenses
2. The Training Rule on Physical Contact At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the Venerable Udāyī was dwelling in the forest.
The dwelling of that venerable one was beautiful, pleasing to behold, and inspiring; it had inner chambers and was surrounded on all sides by a veranda;
the couches, seats, mattresses, and pillows were well-arranged, and drinking water and washing water were well-provided.
The courtyard was well-swept.
Many people came to see the Venerable Udāyī’s dwelling.
Then a certain brahmin, accompanied by his wife, approached the Venerable Udāyī; having approached, he said this to the Venerable Udāyī:
“We wish to see the dwelling of Master Udāyin.
“In that case, brahmin, you may look,” he said;
then, taking his key, opening the latch, and pushing aside the door, he entered the dwelling.
That brahmin entered behind the Venerable Udāyī,
and that brahmin woman entered behind him.
Then the Venerable Udāyī, opening some windows and closing others, went around the inner chamber, came up from behind, and touched the various limbs of that brahmin woman.
Then that brahmin, having exchanged greetings with the Venerable Udāyin, departed.
Then that brahmin, being delighted, uttered these words of delight:
"Noble indeed are these recluses, sons of the Sakyans, who dwell in such a forest as this."
“Venerable Udāyī too is sublime, he who dwells in such a forest.
When this was said, that brahmin woman said this to the brahmin:
“From where does his sublimity come?”
“Just as you touch my limbs, even so does the ascetic Udāyī touch my limbs.
Then that brahmin complained, grumbled, and became indignant:
“These Sakyan-son ascetics are shameless, immoral, and liars!”
"These people indeed claim to be practitioners of the Dhamma, practitioners of equanimity, practitioners of the holy life, speakers of truth, virtuous, and of noble character.
Yet they possess neither the state of a recluse nor the state of a brahmin; their state of a recluse is lost, their state of a brahmin is lost.
Where is their state of a recluse? Where is their state of a brahmin? They have departed from the state of a recluse; they have departed from the state of a brahmin."
"How indeed could the ascetic Udāyī touch the various limbs of my wife?

For it is not possible for women of good family, daughters of good family, young women of good family, daughters-in-law of good family, or female slaves of good family to go to a monastery or a vihāra.

If women of good family, daughters of good family, young women of good family, daughters-in-law of good family, or female slaves of good family were to go to a monastery or a vihāra, those ascetics, sons of the Sakyan, would surely defile them as well."
The monks heard that brahmin complaining, grumbling, and protesting.
Those monks who were of few desires... [and so forth]... they complained, grumbled, and protested:
"How can the Venerable Udāyī engage in physical contact with a woman?"
Then those monks, having rebuked the Venerable Udāyī in many ways, reported this matter to the Blessed One.
Then the Blessed One, on this occasion and in this connection, having assembled the community of monks, questioned the Venerable Udāyī:
“Is it true, Udāyī, that you engaged in physical contact with a woman?”
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him:
“It is unseemly, foolish man, it is unbecoming, improper, unworthy of a recluse, unallowable, and not to be done.”
"How can you, foolish man, engage in physical contact with a woman?
Have I not, foolish man, taught the Dhamma in many ways for the sake of dispassion and not for the sake of passion...
[and so on] ...the subsiding of the fever of sensual desire has been declared?"
“Monk, this does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule:
‘Whatever monk, with a lustful mind, should come into physical contact with a woman, [this is an offense entailing expulsion].’”
“Taking the hand, or taking the braid of hair, or touching any other part of the body, is an offense entailing suspension (saṅghādisesa).
“Whoever,” however, means whoever of such a kind... [and so on].
"Bhikkhu" ...
[as above] ... this is the "bhikkhu" intended in this context.
"One who has entered" (otiṇṇa) means:
One who is lustful, full of longing, and whose mind is bound [to it].
"Transformed" means that even a lustful mind is transformed.
A defiled mind is changed; a deluded mind is also changed.
However, in this context, it is a lustful mind that is intended by the term "changed."
"Woman" means a human female, not a female *yakkha*, not a female *peta*, and not a female animal. At the very least, this includes even a girl born on that same day, let alone one who is older.
"Together with" (*saddhiṃ*).
On one side.
"Should engage in physical contact" is called transgression.
The hand (hattha) is that part beginning from the elbow down to the tips of the nails.
A braid (veṇī) is...
Whether it consists of pure hair, or mixed with thread, or mixed with garlands, or mixed with silver, or mixed with gold, or mixed with pearls, or mixed with gems.
"Limb" means:
setting aside the hand and the braid, the remainder is called a limb.
Touching, stroking, rubbing down, rubbing up, lowering, raising, pulling toward, pulling away, pressing down, squeezing, grasping, and touching.
"Touching" means merely being touched.
"Insulting" means gathering [them] together from here and there.
"Abusing" means...
"Lowering" refers to bringing down from above.
"Sprinkling" (ummasanā) means raising upwards.
"Descending" means bending downward.
"Ascending" means...
"Uddhaṃ" means upward articulation.
"Ākaḍḍhanā" means drawing toward oneself.
"Drawing back" means sending back.
"Restraining" means—
Pressing after grasping a limb.
"Pressing against" means pressing together with something.
"Seizing" means merely having seized.
"Touching" means...
Merely touched.
"Saṅghādisesa" ... [as before] ...
for that reason also it is called "saṅghādisesa."
If there is a woman, he perceives her as a woman, and the monk is lustful;

and he touches her body with his body, strokes it, rubs it down, rubs it up, pushes it down, pushes it up, pulls it toward him, pulls it away, presses it, squeezes it, grasps it, or makes physical contact—there is an offense of *saṅghādisesa*.
If there is a woman, but he is uncertain [of her gender], and he is lustful... [and so on].
If a bhikkhu touches or strokes the body with his own body against that of a woman...
[and so on] ...takes hold of her or makes physical contact, there is an offense of thullaccaya,
provided that she is a woman, he perceives her as a paṇḍaka, and he is lustful.
If a bhikkhu touches or strokes the body with his own body,
or takes hold of or contacts her, it is a thullaccaya offense,
provided that she is a woman, he perceives her as a woman, and he is lustful.
If a bhikkhu touches or strokes the body with his own body against that of a woman... [as before] ...takes hold of her or makes physical contact with her,
there is an offense of thullaccaya,
provided that she is a woman, he perceives her as such, and he is lustful.
If a bhikkhu, with lustful intent, touches or strokes the body of a woman with his own body...

[as before] ...takes hold of her or makes contact with her, there is an offense of thullaccaya. It is also an offense of thullaccaya if he is a paṇḍaka, perceives himself as a paṇḍaka, and is lustful.
If a bhikkhu touches or strokes the body of a paṇḍaka with his own body ... [and so on] ...
takes hold of it or makes contact with it, there is an offense of thullaccaya.
It is a paṇḍaka, but he is uncertain about it, and the bhikkhu is lustful.
If a bhikkhu touches the body with his own body, strokes it, ...
takes hold of it, or touches it against a paṇḍaka, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
And if the paṇḍaka is perceived as a male and the bhikkhu is lustful.
If a bhikkhu touches the body with his body against a paṇḍaka...
[as before] ...takes hold of him, or makes contact with him, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
And the paṇḍaka is perceived by him as an animal, and he is lustful.
If a bhikkhu touches the body with his own body, strokes it, ...
takes hold of it, or touches it against a paṇḍaka—there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
And if the paṇḍaka perceives him as a woman and he is lustful.
If a bhikkhu, with a mind full of lust, touches or strokes the body of a paṇḍaka with his own body...
or takes hold of it or touches it, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
This applies when he is a man and perceives him as a man, and is impassioned.
If the bhikkhu touches or strokes the body with his own body, or takes hold of it, or makes contact with it, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If the man is one about whom he is uncertain... [and so on].
A man perceives [the recipient] as an animal...
a man perceives [the recipient] as a woman...
a man perceives [the recipient] as a paṇḍaka, and he is lustful.
If a bhikkhu, with a mind of lust, touches or strokes the body of an animal with his own body...
or takes hold of it or makes contact with it, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
[This applies when] it is an animal and he perceives it as such, and he is impassioned.
If a bhikkhu touches or strokes the body of an animal with his own body...
or takes hold of it or makes physical contact with it, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If it is an animal and he is in doubt... [and so forth].
He is an animal and perceives her as a woman...
he is an animal and perceives him as a paṇḍaka... he is an animal.
Perceiving it as a human female and being lustful,
if a bhikkhu touches her body with his own body, or strokes it... [as before] ...or takes hold of it or makes contact with it,
there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
The section based on one [factor] is finished.
Two women; perceiving two women as women, he is impassioned.
And a bhikkhu touches body with body, strokes [the bodies] of those two women... [etc. ...
If he takes hold of or touches [them], there is an offense of two *saṅghādisesas*.
If there are two women and he is in doubt regarding those two women, yet he is lustful.
And if a bhikkhu with his own body touches or strokes the body of those two women... [etc.]
If he takes hold of or touches [them], there is an offense of two thullaccayas.
If there are two women and he perceives them as two women, but perceives them as a paṇḍaka...
[or] perceives them as a man... [and so on].
If he perceives her as an animal and is lustful, and a bhikkhu touches or strokes the body with his body against two women ... [as before] ...
takes hold of or contacts them, there is an offense of two thullaccayas.
If there are two paṇḍakas, and a monk, perceiving them as two paṇḍakas and being lustful, touches their bodies with his body, strokes them … [as before] … seizes them or touches them,
he commits two thullaccaya offenses. If there are two paṇḍakas, and he is uncertain whether they are two paṇḍakas … [as before] … [he commits two thullaccaya offenses].
Perceiving him as a man … perceiving him as an animal … perceiving her as a woman,
and being full of lust.
If a monk, with lustful intent, touches or strokes the body of two paṇḍakas with his own body...
or takes hold of them or touches them, there is an offense of two dukkaṭas.
If two men perceive two men as men, and the monk, being lustful, touches or strokes the body of those two men with his own body... [and so forth].
If he takes hold of or touches [them], there is an offense of two *dukkaṭas*.
If there are two men and he is in doubt regarding two men … [and so on] … perceiving them as animals … [and so on].
Perceiving her as a woman...
perceiving him as a paṇḍaka, and being lustful.
And the bhikkhu touches or strokes his body with his body against those two men... [and so forth]...
He takes hold of or touches; there is an offense of two *dukkaṭas*.
Two animals: perceiving them as two animals, he is impassioned.
And if a bhikkhu touches body with body against two animals... [etc. ...he commits an offense.
If he takes hold of or touches [them], there is an offense of two *dukkaṭas*.
If there are two animals and he is in doubt regarding two animals ... [and so on] ...
perceiving them as women ...
Perceiving [the person] as a paṇḍaka...
perceiving [himself] as a man and being lustful.
And the bhikkhu touches body with body against two animals... pe... [as before].
If he takes hold of her and touches her, there is an offense of two *dukkaṭas*.
[The same applies if] a woman and a *paṇḍaka* both perceive each other as women, and the monk is lustful;
and if the monk touches their bodies with his body, or strokes them... [etc.]
If he takes hold of her or touches her, there is an offense of *saṅghādisesa* and an offense of *dukkaṭa*.
[The same applies when] both are a woman and a *paṇḍaka*, and the monk is lustful while being uncertain about both;
and if the monk touches or strokes their bodies with his own body... [etc.]
If he takes hold of her or touches her, there is an offense of thullaccaya and dukkaṭa.
[The case where] both are a woman and a paṇḍaka, and the monk perceives them as both being paṇḍakas, and he is lustful.
If the monk touches their bodies with his body or strokes them … [as before] … pe … [end of formula].
If he takes hold of or touches them, there is an offense of two *thullaccaya*s.
[The case where] both are a woman and a *paṇḍaka*, and the monk perceives both as men and is lustful.
If the monk touches or strokes their bodies with his own body... [etc.]
If he takes hold of her or touches her, there is an offense of thullaccaya and dukkaṭa.
[This applies when] both a woman and a paṇḍaka perceive each other as animals and the bhikkhu is lustful.
If the bhikkhu touches or strokes their bodies with his body... [etc.]
He takes hold of her and touches her; there is an offense of thullaccaya and dukkaṭa.
A woman and a man—perceiving both as such—and he is lustful.
The bhikkhu touches their bodies with his body, or strokes them … [and so forth].
If he takes hold of or touches [her], there is an offense of *saṅghādisesa* and *dukkaṭa*.
If it is a woman and a man, but he is uncertain about both ...
[or] perceives them as a *paṇḍaka* ... [the same applies].
Perceiving [her] as a human woman … perceiving [her] as an animal, and being lustful.
And the bhikkhu touches her body with his own body, strokes it … [and so forth] … *Note: The ellipsis (*pe*) indicates the continuation of the standard formula for bodily contact.*
He takes hold of her and touches her; there is an offense of *thullaccaya* and *dukkaṭa*.
A woman and a being of the animal realm—perceiving both as women, and being lustful.
The monk touches their bodies with his body, or strokes them … [and so forth] …
If he takes hold of her or touches her, there is an offense of *saṅghādisesa* and *dukkaṭa*.
If it is a woman and a non-human animal, and he is in doubt regarding both...
[and so on] ...or perceives them as a *paṇḍaka*...
Perceiving [the woman] as a human being … perceiving her as an animal, and being lustful.

And the bhikkhu touches her body with his own body, or strokes it … [as before] … *Note: This passage is part of the Pācittiya rules concerning sexual misconduct. The full context involves a bhikkhu engaging in physical contact with a woman who is not his wife, under various conditions of perception and intention.*
He takes hold of and touches; there is an offense of *thullaccaya* and *dukkaṭa*.
A *paṇḍaka* and a man—perceiving both as *paṇḍakas* and being lustful—a bhikkhu touches their bodies with his body, strokes them... [etc.]
He takes hold of and touches [him]; there is an offense of thullaccaya and dukkaṭa.
When both the paṇḍaka and the man are objects of doubt … [and so on] … when he perceives him as a man … [and so on].
Perceiving [her] as an animal … perceiving [her] as a woman and being lustful,
the bhikkhu touches her body with his body, strokes it … [and so forth].
If he takes hold of or touches [the body], there is an offense of two *dukkaṭas*.
If it is both a *paṇḍaka* and an animal, and he perceives them as both being *paṇḍakas*, and he is lustful;
and if a monk touches or strokes their bodies with his own body... [etc.]
If one takes hold of or touches [a hermaphrodite], there is an offense of thullaccaya and dukkaṭa.
If it is a paṇḍaka and a tiryagyonigata (animal), and one is in doubt about both... [and so on] ...if one perceives them as a male...

Perceiving [the object] as an animal, or perceiving it as a woman, and being lustful, the bhikkhu touches her body with his own body or strokes it … [as before] … [If he does so] perceiving [her] as a human female … perceiving [her] as a non-human female … perceiving [her] as a male … perceiving [her] as a neuter … perceiving [her] as a hermaphrodite … perceiving [her] as a spirit … perceiving [her] as a hungry ghost … perceiving [her] as a hell-being … perceiving [her] as an animal … perceiving [her] as a human being … perceiving [her] as a non-human being … perceiving [her] as a male … perceiving [her] as a neuter … perceiving [her] as a hermaphrodite … perceiving [her] as a spirit … perceiving [her] as a hungry ghost … perceiving [her] as a hell-being … perceiving [her] as a human female … perceiving [her] as a non-human female … and being lustful,
the bhikkhu touches her body with his own body or strokes it … [as before] …]
If he takes hold of or touches [it], there is an offense of two *dukkaṭas*.
If it is a human male and an animal, and he perceives both as human males, and he is lustful.
If a bhikkhu touches or strokes their bodies with his body... [etc.]
If he takes hold of or touches [it], there is an offense of two *dukkaṭas*.
If both are a human and an animal, and he is uncertain about both … [and so on] … perceiving it as an animal … [and so on].
Perceiving her as a woman … perceiving him as a paṇḍaka, and being lustful,

the bhikkhu touches her body with his own body and strokes it … [and so on] … The bhikkhu perceives her as a woman … perceives him as a paṇḍaka, and is lustful. The bhikkhu touches both of their bodies with his own body and strokes them … [and so on] …
If he takes hold of her or touches her, there is an offense of two *dukkaṭas*.
The section on "Two Roots" is finished.
[The case where] she is a woman, he perceives her as a woman, and he is lustful.
If a bhikkhu, with lustful intent, touches or strokes with his body something connected to the body of a woman...
[and so on] ...takes hold of her or makes physical contact with her, there is an offense of thullaccaya...
[and so on] .... Two women; perceiving two women as women; and he is lustful.
If a bhikkhu, with lustful intent, touches or strokes with his body an object connected to the body of two women with his body...
[as before] ...takes hold of them or touches them, there is an offense of two *thullaccaya*s. ...
[as before] ...A woman and a *paṇḍaka* (eunuch), perceiving both as women, and being lustful.
If the bhikkhu, with his own body, touches or strokes something connected to the body of both [the woman and himself]...
or takes hold of it or makes contact with it, there is an offense of thullaccaya and dukkaṭa... [and so on].
If she is a woman, he perceives her as a woman, and he is lustful.
If a bhikkhu, with lustful intent, touches or strokes the body of a woman with his own body, or ...
takes hold of it or makes physical contact with it, there is an offense of thullaccaya.
... [Omission] ... Two women; perceiving two women as women; and he is lustful.
If a bhikkhu, with a body-part belonging to two women, touches or strokes their bodies … [and so on] … seizes or contacts them,
there is an offense of two *thullaccaya*s … [and so on] ….
If a woman and a *paṇḍaka* both perceive them as women and he is lustful.
If the bhikkhu, with a part of his body connected [to his own], touches or strokes her body with a part of his body connected [to his own]...
takes hold of her or makes contact with her, there is an offense of thullaccaya and dukkaṭa... [and so on].
If she is a woman, he perceives her as a woman, and he is lustful.

If a bhikkhu, with lustful intent, touches or strokes with his own body what is attached to the body of a woman, or takes hold of it, or makes contact with it, there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*). ...
[as before] ... Two women, perceiving two women as such, and he is lustful.
If a bhikkhu, with a body-part connected [to his own], touches or strokes a body-part connected [to another] belonging to two women … pe … takes hold of or contacts them,
there is an offense of two *dukkaṭas* … pe ….
If it is a woman and a *paṇḍaka*, and he perceives both as women, and he is lustful.
If a bhikkhu, with both parties' bodies in contact, touches or strokes the body of the other with his own body...
[and so on] ...takes hold of it or makes physical contact, there is an offense of two *dukkaṭas*... [and so on] ....
If she is a woman, he perceives her as a woman, and he is lustful.

If a bhikkhu, being lustful, touches with his body the body of a woman by means of a limb that is not permissible to relinquish, there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*) … [as before] … Two women,
perceiving them as two women, and he is lustful. If a bhikkhu, being lustful,
touches with his body the bodies of two women by means of limbs that are not permissible to relinquish, there is an offense of wrong-doing for both … [as before] …
If there is both a woman and a paṇḍaka, and perceiving both as women, he is lustful;
and if a bhikkhu touches the body of either with an article that entails relinquishment, there is an offense of wrong-doing for both.
…pe… If there is a woman, and he perceives her as a woman, and he is lustful.
If a bhikkhu touches with his own body, which is not relinquished, something attached to the body of a woman, there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*) … [as before] … Two women,
perceiving them as two women, and he is lustful.
If a bhikkhu touches with his own body, which is not relinquished, something attached to the bodies of two women, there is an offense of two wrong-doings … [as before] …
If there is both a woman and a paṇḍaka, and perceiving both as women, he is lustful;
and if a bhikkhu touches with his body something attached to the body belonging to both by means of an article that entails relinquishment, there is an offense of wrong-doing for both.
…pe… If there is a woman, and he perceives her as a woman, and he is lustful.
If a bhikkhu, being lustful, touches with one thing that is to be relinquished what belongs to a woman and is itself to be relinquished, there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*)... [etc.
...Two women, perceiving two women as such, and he is lustful.
If a bhikkhu, being lustful, touches with one thing that is to be relinquished what belongs to two women and is itself to be relinquished, there is an offense of wrong-doing for both... [etc. ...
If there is a woman and a paṇḍaka, and perceiving both as women, he is lustful;
and if a bhikkhu touches what belongs to both with what belongs to both, there is an offense of two dukkaṭas... [etc.
...The section on bhikkhus is finished.
There is a woman, he perceives her as a woman,
and he is lustful. That woman touches his body with her body, strokes it, rubs it, presses it, pushes it down,
pushes it up, pulls it toward her, pulls it away from her, squeezes it, presses it hard, grasps it, or touches it— with the intention of sexual intercourse.
If he makes an effort with the body and perceives contact, there is an offense entailing suspension (saṅghādisesa) … [as before] … Two women,
perceiving them as two women, being lustful.
And the women touch his body with their bodies, stroke it, rub it, press it, or pull it down.

If one overcomes, pulls toward, pulls away, suppresses, squeezes, seizes, or touches [a woman], with the intention of sexual intercourse, exerts oneself with the body, and experiences contact, there is an offense of two *saṅghādisesas* ... [and so on] ...
when both are a woman and a *paṇḍaka*, and one perceives both as women, and one is lustful.
If both [women] touch and stroke his body with their bodies...
grasp and touch him, and he, with the intention of indulgence, makes an effort with the body and experiences contact, there is an offense of *saṅghādisesa* and *dukkaṭa*... [and so on]...
provided that she is a woman, he perceives her as a woman, and he is lustful.
If a woman touches or strokes a monk’s body, or his body’s appendages, with her own body...
or takes hold of him or touches him; and he, with the intention of indulgence, makes an effort with his body and experiences the contact, there is an offense of *thullaccaya*...
[as before] ... Two women, perceiving two women as women, and he is impassioned.

If women touch or stroke his body, or grasp or brush against it with their own bodies, and he, with the intention of indulgence, makes an effort with his body and experiences contact, he commits two *thullaccaya* offenses... [and so on].
If there is both a woman and a *paṇḍaka*, and he perceives them both as women and is lustful.
If both [women] touch or stroke a monk’s body or anything connected to his body with their own bodies … [as before] … they seize him or touch him;
if he, with the intention of indulgence, makes an effort with the body and experiences contact, there is an offense of a thullaccaya and a dukkaṭa … [as before] … provided that she is a woman,
he perceives her as a woman, and he is lustful.
If a woman touches or strokes his body with her own body connected [to hers]...
or takes hold of him or touches him, and he, with the intention of indulgence, makes an effort with the body and experiences contact, there is an offense of thullaccaya... [and so on].
Two women; perceiving two women as women; and he is impassioned.

If women touch, stroke, grasp, or contact his body with their own bodies, and he—with the intention of indulgence—makes an effort with his body and experiences the contact, there is an offense of two *thullaccaya*s. ...
[as before] ... If both a woman and a *paṇḍaka* are perceived by him as women, and he is lustful.
If both women touch or stroke his body with a part of their own bodies connected to their own bodies...
[as before] ...they seize or contact him; if he, with the intention of indulgence, makes an effort with the body and experiences the contact, there is an offense of a thullaccaya and a dukkaṭa...
[as before] .... And she is a woman, he perceives her as a woman, and he is lustful.
If a woman touches, strokes, takes hold of, or makes contact with a monk’s body by means of her own body,
and he— with the intention of indulgence— exerts himself with the body and experiences the contact, there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*). … [as before] … Two women,
perceiving them as two women, and being lustful.

If women touch, stroke, grasp, or brush against his body with their own bodies, and he, with the intention of indulgence, makes an effort with his body and experiences contact, there is an offense of two *dukkaṭas*... [and so on] ...
If both a woman and a *paṇḍaka* are present, and he perceives them both as women and is lustful.

If both [women] touch or stroke his body with their own bodies, or grasp or contact him, and he, with the intention of indulgence, makes an effort with the body and experiences the contact, there is an offense of two *dukkaṭas*... [and so on].
This applies when there is a woman, he perceives her as a woman, and he is lustful.
If a woman touches his body with something that entails relinquishment, and he, with the intention of indulgence,
makes an effort with his body and perceives the contact, there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*) … [as before] … Two women,
perceiving two women as women, and he is impassioned.
If women touch his body with an article that must be relinquished, and he,
with the intention of pursuing [sexual] gratification, makes an effort with the body and experiences contact, there is an offense of two *dukkaṭas*...
[and so on] ...if a woman and a *paṇḍaka* both perceive them as women and he is lustful.
Both touch his body with an article that entails relinquishment. If, with the intention of indulgence,
he makes an effort with the body and perceives contact, there is an offense of two *dukkaṭas* … [and so on] … It is a woman,
he perceives her as a woman, and he is lustful.
If a woman touches with her own body something attached to the body of a bhikkhu that is subject to relinquishment,
and he, with the intention of indulgence, makes an effort with his body and perceives the contact, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa) … [as before] … Two women,
perceiving two women as women, and he is impassioned.
If women touch a monk’s article that must be relinquished which is attached to his body, and he,

with the intention of pursuing [sexual] gratification, makes an effort with the body and experiences contact, there is an offense of two *dukkaṭas* … [and so on] … If it is both a woman and a *paṇḍaka*,
and he perceives both as women, and he is lustful.
If both women touch what is attached to the body of a monk with an article that entails relinquishment,
and he, with the intention of indulgence, makes an effort with his body and perceives contact, there is an offense of two *dukkaṭas*...
[and so on] ...if there is a woman, he perceives her as a woman, and he is lustful.
If a woman touches what is subject to relinquishment with what is subject to relinquishment for a bhikkhu;
he, with the intention of pursuing [sexual intercourse], makes an effort with the body, but does not perceive contact— there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*) … [as before] … Two women,
perceiving two women as women, and he is impassioned.
If women touch a monk’s article that has been relinquished with an article that has been relinquished,

and he, with the intention of indulgence, makes an effort with his body but does not perceive contact, there is an offense of two *dukkaṭas* … [and so on] … If a woman and a *paṇḍaka* both have the perception of a woman, and he is lustful.

If both touch what belongs to a monk with what belongs to a monk by way of relinquishment, and he makes an effort with the body with the intention of pursuing [sexual intercourse], but does not perceive contact, there is an offense of wrong-doing for both. ...
If he makes an effort with the body with the intention of pursuing [sexual intercourse] and perceives contact, there is an offense entailing suspension (saṅghādisesa).
If one makes an effort with the body with the intention of engaging in sexual intercourse, but does not experience physical contact, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If one has the intention of engaging in sexual intercourse but does not make an effort with the body, yet experiences physical contact, there is no offense.
If one has the intention of engaging in sexual intercourse but neither makes an effort with the body nor experiences physical contact, there is no offense.
If one strives with the body with the intention of liberation and perceives contact, there is no offense.
If one strives with the body with the intention of liberation but does not perceive contact, there is no offense.
If one does not strive with the body but perceives contact with the intention of liberation, there is no offense.
If one aims for liberation, but does not exert oneself with the body nor perceive contact, there is no offense.
There is no offense if it was unintentional.

For one who is insane,

2.1. Summary Verse on the Basis for Discipline:
Mother, daughter, and sister.
A wife, a female spirit, and a paṇḍaka;
those who are asleep, the dead, animals,
and one who is like a wooden doll.
In the crush, the path is a narrow crossing;
there is a tree, a boat, and a rope;
the staff pushed away the bowl.
"I pay homage; I do not touch her.
2.2. The Case of Vinīta:
Now at that time, a certain monk touched his mother out of maternal affection.
He became anxious, thinking:
"A training rule has been laid down by the Blessed One;
could it be that I have fallen into an offense involving formal meeting (saṅghādisesa)?"
He reported this matter to the Blessed One.
"There is no offense of *saṅghādisesa*, monk;
there is an offense of *dukkaṭa*," [the Blessed One said].
Now at that time, a certain bhikkhu touched his daughter out of affection for his daughter...
[and] he touched his sister out of affection for his sister.
He became anxious... [as before].
“There is no offense, monk, against the *saṅghādisesa*;
there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
Now at that time, a certain monk engaged in physical contact with his former wife.
He felt remorse... [as before] ...
"Bhikkhu, you have committed an offense entailing suspension (saṅghādisesa).
Now at that time, a certain bhikkhu engaged in physical contact with a female yakkha.
He became anxious... [as before] ...
"There is no offense of *saṅghādisesa*, monk;
there is an offense of *thullaccaya*."
Now at that time, a certain bhikkhu engaged in physical contact with a paṇḍaka.
He became anxious... [as before] ...
"There is no offense, bhikkhu, entailing a formal meeting of the Saṅgha."
“There is an offense of thullaccaya.
Now at that time, a certain bhikkhu engaged in physical contact with a woman who had just bathed.
He became anxious... [as before]...
“You have committed an offense, monk, entailing suspension (saṅghādisesa).
Now at that time, a certain monk engaged in physical contact with a dead woman.
He became anxious... [as before]...
“There is no offense of *saṅghādisesa*, monk;
there is an offense of *thullaccaya*.
Now at that time, a certain monk engaged in physical contact with a female animal.
He became anxious... [as before] ...
"There is no offense, monk, against the *saṅghādisesa*;
there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*)."
Now at that time, a certain monk engaged in bodily contact with a wooden doll.
He became anxious... [as before] ...
"There is no offense, monk, for a *saṅghādisesa*."
“There is an offense of wrong-doing.
Now at that time, several women crowded around a certain bhikkhu and led him along by passing their arms from one to another.
He became anxious... [as before]...
“Did you consent, monk?
“I did not consent, Blessed One.
“There is no offense, monk, for one who does not consent.”
Now at that time, a certain bhikkhu, being lustful, shook a bridge on which a woman was mounted.
He felt remorse... [as before] ...
"There is no offense, bhikkhu, of *saṅghādisesa*."
“There is an offense of wrong-doing.
Now at that time, a certain monk, having seen a woman on the opposite path, being lustful, struck her with his shoulder-blade.
He became anxious... [as before]...
“You have committed an offense, monk, entailing suspension (saṅghādisesa).
Now at that time, a certain monk, being lustful, shook a tree mounted upon by a woman.
He became anxious... [as before]...
“There is no offense, monk, against the *saṅghādisesa*;
there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
Now at that time, a certain monk, being lustful, shook a boat that a woman had boarded.
He felt remorse... [as before] ...
"There is no offense of *saṅghādisesa*, monk;
there is an offense of *dukkaṭa*."
Now at that time, a certain bhikkhu, being lustful, pulled a rope held by a woman.
He felt remorse... [as before] ...
"There is no offense, bhikkhu, of *saṅghādisesa*."
“There is an offense of thullaccaya.
Now at that time, a certain monk, being lustful, pulled a stick held by a woman.
He became anxious... [as before]...
“There is no offense of *saṅghādisesa*, monk;
there is an offense of *thullaccaya*.
Now at that time, a certain monk, being lustful, sent away a woman with his alms-bowl.
He became anxious... [as before] ...
"There is no offense of *saṅghādisesa*, monk;
there is an offense of *thullaccaya*."
Now at that time, a certain bhikkhu, being lustful, raised his foot when a woman was bowing down to him.
He became anxious... [as before] ...
"Bhikkhu, you have fallen into an offense entailing suspension (saṅghādisesa)."
Now at that time, a certain bhikkhu, having made an effort thinking, "I will take hold of a woman," did not touch her.
He became anxious... [as before] ...
"There is no offense, bhikkhu, of *saṅghādisesa*."
“There is an offense of wrong-doing.
The second training rule on physical contact is finished.
